transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’ve lost the drive to do anything or be around people, and it’s getting harder and harder to talk or care about things the way I used to. Most days I just don't have the energy to do much of anything anymore.
Have you recently had any unusual experiences, like hearing voices when you're alone, or feeling like others are watching or plotting against you?

I don't hear any voices, but over the last couple of months, I've felt like people are watching me. I'm pretty sure the ladies at church and the clinic nurses are checking up on me, pausing their conversations and talking in code to monitor what I'm doing.
Have you ever had times when your mood and energy felt completely back to normal, but you still felt like people were watching you or talking in code?

No, my energy and drive haven't gone back to normal at all; I've felt shut down like this continuously for over two years now. The feeling that people are watching me and talking in code is much newer, only starting in the last couple of months.
Besides having low energy and drive, have you also been feeling deeply sad, or experiencing strong feelings of worthlessness or guilt during this time?
No, I wouldn't say I feel deeply sad or guilty. It's more that I just feel completely blank inside, like there's nothing there. I just don't have the drive to care about anything anymore.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being broadcast out loud so others can hear them, or that someone is putting thoughts into your head that aren't your own?
No, I've never felt like my thoughts were being broadcasted out loud for others to hear. And I don't feel like anyone else is putting thoughts into my head, either.
Have family members or friends mentioned that it's hard to follow your conversation because your thoughts seem jumbled or you jump from topic to topic?
No, my family hasn't ever said my thoughts seem jumbled or that I jump around. It's more that I just feel blank inside and don't have much to say, so my conversations are usually very short.
Have you been using any recreational drugs, drinking alcohol, or taking any new medications, especially around the time you started feeling like people were watching you?
No, I don't drink alcohol or use any drugs at all. I'm also not taking any medications right now.

No further differential diagnoses are highly probable, so the interview can be finalized.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with prominent negative symptoms (avolition, flat affect, alogia, and social withdrawal) that have been continuously present for over two years, alongside more recently developed persecutory and referential delusions (believing church members and clinic nurses are monitoring them and speaking in code) of a couple of months' duration. There is no evidence of a major mood episode, organic etiology, or substance use, which fits the clinical picture of Schizophrenia (F20).
